height_zero.proof: Write y=u+phi*v.  If y^2 is the rational canonical norm q, then u^2+v^2=q and 2(u.v)+v^2=0.  Minimum three excludes q=1,2.  Before the 3-adic gate the only surviving binary Gram types for q=3,6 are (3,0,0) and (6,0,0).  The gate puts u and v in the mod-three pairing radical, whose certified minimum is at least seven, so both types are excluded.  Hence height zero is empty for both timelike coefficients.

norm_alphabet.proof: The primes 2 and 3 are inert in Z[phi], the class number is one, and the totally-positive units are precisely the even powers of phi, hence unit squares.  For a primitive root r=(x,y), reflection integrality is (q(r))|2I(r), I(r)=(a*x,(y,S23)).  Since S23 has Smith invariants 1^22,3, every prime away from 2, 3, and the coefficient would divide both x and y, contradicting primitivity.  For a=phi the coefficient is a unit, so v_2(q)<=v_2(2)=1.  For a=2*phi, either y has a unit pairing and the same bound holds, or y lies in 2*S23; then primitivity makes x a 2-adic unit and q=-2*phi*x^2 mod 4, so v_2(q)=1.  At 3, positive q-valuation forces x into (3) and both coefficients of y into the one-dimensional pairing radical modulo 3.  Its primitive pairing ideal has valuation exactly one, so v_3(q)<=1.  Thus, modulo totally-positive unit-square scaling, the complete norm alphabet for both coefficients is 1,2,3,6.  In the last two classes both spatial coefficients lie in the mod-three pairing radical.
norm_alphabet.three_gate_radical_exclusion: In the displayed section basis, ker(G mod 3) is generated by the last coordinate, whose raw vector is (-23,1^23), congruent to (1^24) mod 3. Thus every vector in the pairing radical has all raw coordinates congruent mod 3. Raw norm 3 means square sum 24: residue 0 is impossible, while residue +/-1 forces all coordinates +/-1 with one common sign, contradicting coordinate sum zero. Raw norms 4 and 5 have square sums 32 and 40. In a nonzero residue class, common odd parity makes every coordinate equal to the least representative +/-1 unless the square sum is already at least 48, contradicting sum zero; common even parity has square sum at least 96. Residue zero is impossible modulo 9. For raw norm 6, square sum 48. Residue 0 is again impossible. Writing a residue-1 coordinate as 1+3k, the zero-sum and square-sum equations give sum(k)=-8 and sum(k^2)=8, hence exactly eight coordinates are -2 and sixteen are 1; this violates the common coordinate parity of every odd-Leech vector. Residue -1 is the negative case. Therefore the radical has no vector of norm at most 6 (in particular no norm 3 or 6 vector).

norm_4.proof: On the raw sqrt(8) scale, norm four means square 32 and coordinate sum zero.  In the even coset write the vector as 2t.  The equation t^2=8 has only two Golay-compatible parity supports: weight eight, giving 759*C(8,4)=53130 sign-balanced octad vectors, and weight zero, giving 24*23=552 ordered choices of one +4 and one -4 raw coordinate.  In the odd coset square 32 would mean one coordinate of absolute value three and 23 of absolute value one.  Flipping that coordinate changes a Golay sign-word sum by plus or minus four, which would require codeword weight 10 or 14; neither exists.  Thus the complete section shell has 53682 vectors.

norm_5.proof: On the raw sqrt(8) scale, norm five means square 40 and coordinate sum zero.  In the even coset, after division by two, every partition of ten into squares has odd-coordinate support of weight 2, 6, or 10, none a Golay weight.  In the odd coset exactly two coordinates have absolute value three and the other 22 have absolute value one.  Relative to a Golay sign word, the two large coordinates reverse sign.  Zero sum allows: two zero positions for weight 8, one zero and one one position for weight 12, or two one positions for weight 16.  Hence the complete count is 759*C(16,2)+2576*12*12+759*C(16,2)=553104.
